speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Singapore is a trusted, vibrant and well-regulated international financial centre in Asia, one of the fastest growing regions in the world.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Naturally, this has attracted a wide range of investors, including global and regional institutional investors as well as individual investors.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Family offices are one particular category of individual investment.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) does not have comprehensive data on fund inflows into Singapore through family offices.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Such detailed data is not necessary for MAS to carry out its functions of ensuring macroeconomic and financial stability.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Louis Chua asked about wealth flows while Mr Leong Mun Wai asked about foreign funds inflow through family offices.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I take their interest to be in investments made by high-end individual investors.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The investor type closest to high-end individual investors in MAS’ annual Asset Management Survey is the category called “non-retail individual clients”.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This category includes family offices, clients of external asset managers, private trusts and high net worth individuals.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This makes up about 20% of the increase in total AUM by Singapore’s asset management industry from 2017 to 2021.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Also, the growth of assets from these high-end individual clients has been broadly similar to that for overall AUM.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This, in other words, means that there has been a much broader pick-up of funds flowing into Singapore’s wealth management industry, but it is not peculiar to these high-end individual clients.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In short, the bulk of the increase in AUM in Singapore is attributable to institutional investors.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Non-retail individual clients account for a small proportion, and family offices even less.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Louis Chua and Mr Leong Mun Wai asked for a breakdown by source countries of wealth inflows, and for Mr Leong Mun Wai, specifically for family offices.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Based on the Asset Management Survey, non-retail individual clients come from a wide range of places.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The most granular breakdown of foreign sourced funds is available by regions, rather than by specific countries.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This is no different from surveys published by financial sector authorities or industry associations in major wealth management centres like London, Hong Kong and Switzerland.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: What we are providing on the regional breakdown for non-retail individual clients in fact goes beyond what these other jurisdictions publish as they do not put out data on specific categories of investors like individual investors.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The top-sourced foreign region for the increase in Singapore’s AUM for high-end individual investors from that period of 2017 to 2021 was the Asia Pacific, as is to be expected.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This accounted for slightly over half of AUM sourced from high-end individual investors.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Asia-Pacific was followed by Europe and the Americas.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Leong asked how much SFOs that have applied for tax incentives since April 2022 have invested in local investments.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We do not yet have the data as these SFOs have two years from their point of application to meet the local investments requirement that MAS just introduced in April 2022 – so, just one year ago.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We are within the first two-year implementation period, so, data on the volume of assets is not currently available.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Members of the House should note, however, that while assets are managed in Singapore by entities based in Singapore, most of these assets are invested outside Singapore.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And this is understandable as the investment universe is much larger outside Singapore and investors use Singapore as a financial centre to access investment opportunities in our region and beyond.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: But as these assets are managed from Singapore, they help to create jobs and valued-added in our financial industry.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: There are also positive spill-overs to other sectors as these investors often appoint tax and legal professionals for wealth planning and operational matters.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, it benefits our financial industry and beyond.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Leong Mun Wai also asked about the impact of the inflow of foreign funds through family offices on our Official Foreign Reserves (OFRs), the private property market and inflation.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The bulk of the gross inflows into Singapore comprise flows by financial institutions and other non-financial corporates, not high-end individual investors; and even less so family offices which are only one category within the latter.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: To reiterate, most of the funds managed here are invested in assets outside Singapore.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Hence, they typically remain in foreign currencies – this is to the second point about the impact on OFRs.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, most funds are managed here, are invested outside and they also typically remain in foreign currencies and thus, have little or no effect on the Singapore dollar exchange rate or our OFRs.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: If some of these inflows do get converted into Singapore dollars, they would, just like all net capital flows into Singapore dollars, generate some appreciation pressure on the exchange rate.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The third question by Mr Leong Mun Wai is on the impact on inflation.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: As for inflation, it has little to do with foreign fund inflows into Singapore, let alone the portion due to family offices.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And now, the impact on the private property market.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Some foreign funds do flow into the private property market.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: However, purchases by foreigners have been relatively low, at about 4% of all private residential property purchases on average over the past three years.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The first is in relation to my Parliamentary Question (PQ).

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I understand the Minister of State's point about the level of granularity provided, but I was just wondering in relation to the 14 April press release by MAS, it did state that the source of overall inflows into Singapore is diversified.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: So, I was just wondering if there is any further granularity that the Minister of State can provide to assure the public of the level of dispersion or concentration risks of any particular source country?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Second, in relation to the PQ which was filed by Mr Leong Mun Wai, I also understand that at this point in time, because they are not at the two-year mark as mentioned by the Minister of State, we do not yet have that data.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: In terms of the level of local investment requirement, I recognise that this is indeed a good thing, but given that, as the Minister of State mentioned, most of it would presumably be invested in overseas markets, in overseas assets.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Is there a push by the Government or MAS to, over time, nudge some of these companies to invest in local companies a little bit more, especially in the last category, when it comes to non-listed Singapore-incorporated companies, since these tend to give a greater multiplier effect —

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Chua, can I ask you to wrap it up?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We have given more details because, as I mentioned earlier on, of those centres that publish surveys quite similar to our MAS survey that I mentioned, none of the surveys published source country details.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Some also do not even publish regional breakdowns.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I think that would suffice in terms of source country breakdown.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: With regard to the second question, I think I had responded to one of the Member's questions with regard to the requirements for SFO.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We are still within the two-year period, so I encourage the Member and other Members of this House to ask again after the two-year period.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Actually, we should clarify that the response was that the two PQs yesterday that were filed would be answered via Minister of State Alvin Tan's response today together with Mr Louis Chua's PQ.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: It was made known that the responses would be made today.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Oh, yes, yes, it was in the Written Circular.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: I wanted to be clear that there was not any avoidance in terms of answering the questions.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The Minister of State's answer mainly centred on the family office.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Of course, I mean that is how I had phrased the question as well.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, I do not know whether it is fair to ask him now to answer one supplementary question on what is the impact of the total foreign inflow on our OFRs?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: On top of the family office, everything, for the last two to three years.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The first is that we have every intention of answering those questions.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The Member has reached out to me also.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And specifically, the Member did not put it in time for it to be rolled over and so it was converted to Written PQs.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And the team had very specifically noted that we wanted to answer both questions by Mr Louis Chua as well as Mr Leong Mun Wai as comprehensively as possible, which I had done so.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The Member's questions on foreign funds inflow, it was specific to SFOs.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, if you wanted an answer to a broader question with regards to overall foreign funds inflow, may I ask the Member to file a separate PQ, which we will be happy to take at another Sitting.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: If I heard him correctly, he said that foreigners accounted for 4% of private property transactions in the last three years.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Can I clarify – does that classify Permanent Residents (PRs) as foreigners?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: And up until what point is this data available?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I mean, is it as at the end of last year and we are counting the last three years from the end of last year backwards or so on?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Maybe, just let me give the Member a broader view.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Again, the Member wanted more questions, I would ask the Member to file a separate PQ on foreign housing.
